text: During the whole of a dull, dark, and soundless autumn day, I had been riding alone on horseback through a dreary stretch of country. <break time="0.8s" /> At last, as the evening shadows drew on, I found myself within view of the gloomy House of Usher, the home of my old friend. <break time="0.8s" /> I do not know why, but with the first glimpse of the building, a feeling of unbearable gloom filled my spirit. <break time="0.8s" /> I looked upon the bare walls, the empty, eye like windows, and a few white trunks of dead trees, and my heart sank. <break time="0.8s" /> Hoping to change the sad effect of the scene, I rode my horse to the edge of a black, silent tarn beside the house. <break time="0.8s" /> But looking down at the upside down image of the house in the water, I felt a shudder even stronger than before. <break time="0.8s" /> Its owner, Roderick Usher, had been one of my closest companions in boyhood, but many years had passed since our last meeting. <break time="0.8s" /> Recently a letter had reached me from him, in which he wrote of an illness of body and mind and begged me to visit him. <break time="0.8s" /> Studying the house more closely, I noticed a barely visible crack, which ran from the roof down the wall in a zigzag line into the dark water.
